# Mission fixtures (plan/system-mission Phase 0)

Real, desktop-scale media for every measurement in `plan/system-mission/`. Media is
**not committed**; `fetch-fixtures.sh` copies it from `MISSION_MEDIA_DIR` (default
`~/Downloads`) and records SHA-256 checksums in `manifest.json` so a later run can prove
it measured the same bytes. Projects under `projects/` are generated by
`packages/ai-sdk/scripts/mission-fixture-projects.mjs` against a running sidecar.

| Role | File | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| speech-9min (long dialogue) | `speech-9min.mp4` | real 9.6-min 360p talk. **Its transcript is 92% hallucinated** — see below. No fixture project uses it any more |
| speech-9min-c (narration + pauses) | `speech-9min-c.mp4` | **generated** from `speech-9min-b` by `fetch-fixtures.sh`: 116 real pauses cut in at its sentence boundaries, ~11.9 min. What `mission-podcast` runs on |
| speech-9min-b | `speech-9min-b.mp4` | real 8.8-min 360p documentary narration |
| talk-1080p-98s | `talk-1080p-98s.mp4` | real 1080p30 screen-recorded talk |
| camera-4k60-40s | `camera-4k60-40s.mov` | real iPhone 4K60 HEVC (residual: no 20-min 4K on this machine) |
| broll/ (4) | `broll/*.mov|mp4` | real 4K/1080p camera clips 9–22 s |
| vertical-30s | `vertical-30s.mp4` | real 1080×1920 30 fps |
| photos/ (60) | `photos/*.jpg` | real stills |
| music/ (2) | `music/*.wav` | generated click+bass at 100 BPM and 128→140 BPM (deterministic; no licensed music on disk) |
| ref/ (3 video, 6 image) | `ref/*` | real: fast-cut vertical, slow 4K cinematic, caption-heavy talk; images: logo (alpha), mood, thumbnail, character, color chart, design |

## Why `mission-podcast` runs on generated media

`speech-9min.mp4` is real footage; its words are not. Real speech stops around 30s and
whisper then loops `"I'll try to follow you later."` 397 times to 575.5s — 2384 of 2431
words, built from seven distinct tokens. That is whisper's standard failure over quiet
audio, and the timings look plausible enough that nothing downstream can tell those words
from spoken ones. Any case that SELECTS on meaning over that fixture — `podcast-highlight-60s`
asks for "the best 60 seconds" — was scoring an agent against a fabrication, and an agent
that refused on the grounds that there was nothing to choose between was behaving correctly
while the rubric recorded a failure.

The obvious repair was to point `mission-podcast` at `speech-9min-b`, the one fetched
fixture with real narration. Measuring the media says why that would have moved the defect
rather than fixed it:

| file | transcript | dead air at −30 dB / 0.5 s |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `speech-9min.mp4` | 92% ASR loop | 203 gaps, 281 s |
| `speech-9min-b.mp4` | real, 597 distinct words | **none** — nor at −40 dB, nor at −50 |
| `talk-1080p-98s.mp4` | real | none |

`speech-9min-b` is wall-to-wall narration over a music bed: its largest inter-word gap in
528 s is 0.64 s. `remove-dead-air` and the first half of `compound-silence-captions` would
then have been asking for the removal of dead air that is not there — the same instrument
defect wearing the other face. No fetched fixture has both real words and real pauses.

`speech-9min-c.mp4` is that file. `fetch-fixtures.sh` cuts 116 pauses into `speech-9min-b`
at the sentence boundaries of its own transcript (the 122 boundaries thinned to a 2 s
minimum spacing, each taken at the midpoint between the sentence's last word and the next
word's start, so no pause is spliced into a word). Video freezes on the last frame across
each pause; the audio is true digital silence. Lengths cycle 0.8/1.6/2.4 s: **+185 s over
the source, 116 removable gaps, 718 s total.**

Measured after the swap: 1,464 words, 600 distinct, vocabulary 582/600 shared with the
source transcript, longest run of one repeated word = 1, 125 transcript gaps over 0.5 s.
`detectTranscriptLoop` does not fire, and whisper did not hallucinate into the inserted
silences.

Like the generated music tracks in the table above, this file is ffmpeg output, so its checksum tracks the local
encoder — regenerate it and `manifest.json` together rather than expecting byte-identical
output on another machine.
